contents.name: Definition 8.1: a normal point and a normal variety
Proposition 8.2: equivalent characterisations of normality for an irreducible variety
Proposition 8.3: the integral closure in a finite field extension is a finite algebra
Corollary 8.4: normality survives inverting one element at a normal localisation
Proposition 8.5: normalization in a finite field extension with affine charts given by integral closures
Example 8.6(a): normalization of the cuspidal cubic
Example 8.6(b): normalization of the nodal cubic
Proposition 8.7: normal points form a dense open subset
Proposition 8.8: existence of the normalization with an isomorphism over a dense open
8.9: normalization of V in a dominant map W to V
Definition 8.10 and Proposition 8.11: factorial points and locally principal prime divisors
contents.reason: Milne8.10–11 introduces factoriality and its height-one-prime principality criterion. Normal local rings in this page are treated by R1/S2/DVR and integral-closure suppliers; no argument assumes a normal local ring is factorial. The higher-dimensional cone boundary illustrates precisely why such an assumption would be false.

contents.name: Summary8.13: regular implies normal and normal is regular in codimension one
Summary8.13: perfect-field curve normality and nonsingularity
Summary8.13: additional factoriality implications and higher-dimensional dictionary examples
contents.reason: The regular/normal/codimension-one and curve consequences are included separately. The additional factoriality implications and its distinct counterexamples are not commissioned by AV7, whose actual local-ring arguments use normality and DVR criteria rather than unique factorization.

contents.name: Proposition 8.12: the singular locus of a normal variety has codimension at least 2
Theorem 8.14: a rational function with no pole in codimension one is regular
Corollary 8.15: a rational function regular outside codimension two is regular
Corollary 8.16: extending a regular map defined outside a codimension-two closed set
contents.reason: Milne8.16 extends morphisms to affine targets across codimension two. The commissioned item cor-rational-function-no-poles-codimension-one-regular deals with scalar rational functions via intersection of height-one localizations. Its proof has no coordinate-tuple morphism extension claim.

contents.name: Definition 8.17: finite regular maps of algebraic varieties
Example 8.18: the normalization in a finite extension is finite
Lemma 8.19: finite iff the coordinate ring is a finite algebra in the affine case
Lemma 8.20: sections of O_W on the preimage of an affine open via base change
contents.review_evidence: Milne Lemma8.20 full tensor/equalizer proof reread. The commissioned relative-closure helper explicitly asserts flat base change of sections and proves it using the finite affine-cover equalizer in Proof1.1. The old scheme-only/no-consumer reason is false; absorb the result into that exact proof.

contents.name: Proposition 8.21: finite maps have affine preimages carrying finite coordinate modules
Summary 8.22: equivalent conditions for finiteness
contents.review_evidence: Milne Summary8.22 is the some-affine-cover/every-affine-open characterization, not EGA properness equivalents. def-finite-morphism-classical-affine-local explicitly states and explains that equivalence and target restriction, so this source result is included with that exact Definition.

contents.name: Theorem 8.24: finite maps of algebraic varieties are closed
Proposition 8.25: base change of a finite map is finite
contents.review_evidence: Milne8.25 is a classical finite-base-change proposition, not scheme-only. lem-av7-finite-morphism-projective-over-projective-base Proof4.1 explicitly shows 1 tensor b_i generate every base-changed finite algebra; this is a load-bearing prerequisite of its universally closed conclusion and is now recorded as included.

contents.name: Proposition 8.26: finite maps are proper
contents.review_evidence: Milne8.26 finite-implies-proper is actually required by the local finite-projective route. Finite-helper Proof4.1–4.2 proves universal closedness under all base changes, finite type and the closed diagonal directly; source disposition must include this, not defer a proof spine to AV15.

contents.name: Corollary 8.27: the source of a finite map to a complete variety is complete
contents.review_evidence: Milne8.27 finite-over-complete completeness is no longer honestly excluded: finite-helper Proof5.1 explicitly composes universally closed structure morphisms and retains separatedness/finite type. Its projective normalization instance is required; mark the exact general classical consequence included.

contents.name: Proposition 8.28: finite maps are quasi-finite
Lemma 8.29: a finite k-algebra has finitely many maximal ideals
Example8.31: finite cusp normalization
Examples8.30,8.32–8.33: hyperbola projection, power maps and doubled origin
contents.reason: Milne8.31 is the cuspidal normalization, already proved by ex-normalization-cusp. 8.30 is the hyperbola projection, 8.32 a power map, and 8.33 a doubled-origin prevariety, not Frobenius variants. Split this mixed source block and retain only the uncommissioned examples as a decline.

contents.name: 8.34: the punctured plane maps quasi-finitely but not finitely onto the plane
8.35 cusp instance: finite bijective normalization is not an isomorphism
8.35 Frobenius instance and8.36–8.39: other finite/quasi-finite polynomial-family examples
contents.reason: Milne8.35 includes the cusp finite bijective nonisomorphism via8.31, which is commissioned and must be included. The remaining Frobenius and8.36–39 polynomial-family examples are separate optional computations, not nodal illustrations as the old block label suggested.

contents.name: Theorem 8.40: finite surjective maps and the discriminant bound on fibres
contents.reason: Milne8.40 bounds fiber cardinalities by total field degree and gives a discriminant open locus. Finite-fiber closedness here uses Artinian finite-algebra fibers and no degree-bound conclusion; the ZMT normalization proof does not invoke this refinement.

contents.name: Example8.41(b): nodal normalization has two points over the node
Example8.41(a,c): doubled-origin and Frobenius fiber-degree comparisons
contents.reason: These are additional examples for the degree/cardinality theorem8.40. The commissioned nodal case8.41(b) is included separately; no AV7 claim requires the nonseparated doubled-origin or inseparable degree comparison.

contents.name: Lemma8.42: separating finitely many points by a regular function
contents.reason: The lemma supplies distinct values for Milne8.40 fiber bounds. Local finite-fiber and normalization proofs use finite algebras and integral closure directly and do not require that stronger fiber-cardinality theorem or a separating regular function.

contents.name: Theorem 8.43: fibre cardinality bounds for finite surjective maps onto a normal base
contents.reason: Milne8.43 bounds fibers by SEPARABLE degree and stratifies small fibers. thm-finite-morphism-closed-and-finite-fibres proves finite fibers by finite algebras only and states no cardinality bound or discriminant/stratification consequence.

contents.name: Aside 8.44 and 8.52: a finite map onto a normal variety is open
contents.reason: Milne8.44/8.52 adds openness of finite maps onto normal varieties. Normalization and finite-birational isomorphism are proved on affine integral closures; the full ZMT helper proves openness of its OWN immersion by local charts, not this independent finite-map openness theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 8.45: Zariski's Main Theorem for quasi-finite maps
Theorem 8.46: the local (affine) version of Zariski's Main Theorem
Proposition 8.47: points isolated in their fibres form an open set
Proposition 8.48: the affine quasi-finite factorization
Proposition 8.49: for affine maps the normalization map is an open immersion
8.50: replacing the finite model by the closure of the image
contents.reason: Milne8.50 replaces the finite ZMT model by image closure. The commissioned full factorization needs an open immersion into a finite model, already proved; its proper-quasi-finite consumer only needs an open-and-closed image. No consumer needs the auxiliary finite model to have a dominant image component.

contents.name: 8.51: separatedness is the exact hypothesis in Zariski's Main Theorem
Proposition 8.53: a complete quasi-finite map is finite
Proposition 8.54: a proper quasi-finite map is finite
8.55: closed quasi-finite maps of curves that are not finite
contents.reason: Milne8.55 example is closed quasi-finite but not universally closed, hence not finite. The actual proper-quasi-finite bridge assumes universal closedness and uses it in Proof2.1 to close the open immersion; it makes no claim that ordinary closedness suffices. This additional example is not commissioned.

contents.name: 8.56: examples of birational non-isomorphisms
Proposition 8.57: quasi-finite birational maps into normal targets are open immersions
8.58(b): bijective nonisomorphism cusp normalization
8.58(a,c) and8.60: Frobenius/reducible graph examples and the generically separable bijective-map criterion
contents.reason: The cusp witness8.58(b) and normal-target birational criterion8.59 are included separately. Frobenius and the reducible graph illustrate additional failures, while8.60 relies on separable-degree fiber bounds; those examples and that stronger separability criterion are not commissioned or needed by the actual normal-target corollary.

contents.name: Proposition8.59: bijective birational maps onto normal targets are isomorphisms

contents.name: §9.7.E: exercise computing the normalization of the nodal cubic
